sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Henderson County?
sections.html:
Property tax in this county runs on two desks. An Assessor sets values here, and a Tax Collector bills and collects. The collector's counter is Suite 66, ground floor, at 200 North Grove Street, Hendersonville, NC 28792, open weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00.

For an appraisal or appeal, dial 828-697-4667. For payments, dial 828-697-5595. Rates are not the Assessor's call: commissioners and the governing bodies of Hendersonville, Fletcher, Saluda, Mills River, Flat Rock and Laurel Park each set one to fit their budgets.

One collector bills for the county, thirteen fire districts, Hendersonville, Laurel Park and the Henderson County portion of Saluda. The Assessor's page counts 22 tax districts, including the general county district, and rates vary with the services each district provides.

sections.h2: How does Henderson County value property?
sections.html:
Everything taxable is valued at 100% of market value under the uniform standards in G.S. 105-283. The workload covers about 71,500 parcels, some 4,500 businesses with personal property, over 10,000 manufactured homes and more than 100,000 registered vehicles that are billed monthly.

Henderson County reappraises every four years rather than waiting for the eight-year state limit in G.S. 105-286. The last reappraisal was in 2023, and the next takes effect January 1, 2027. Buildings still under construction on January 1 are valued by their percent complete, and a farm or forest tract in the Present-Use Value Program is assessed below market.

The county's reappraisal page estimates that property tax covers 50% of total operating spending in fiscal year 2027.

sections.h2: What is the Henderson County 2027 reappraisal schedule?
sections.html:
The county's published schedule runs from the Schedule of Values hearing in fall 2026 through tax bills in August 2027. Notices of assessed value are expected to go out around February 1, 2027, so owners will see new numbers before the appeal window closes.

Source: Henderson County Reappraisal Schedule. The county also lists information sessions for community groups from September 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027.

sections.h2: What steps does a Henderson County appeal follow?
sections.html:
An informal written appeal to the Assessor comes first, on the county's standard form. A formal appeal goes to the county review board only when that fails to settle the value, and it must be received before the board adjourns.

  • Once a formal appeal is in, an appraiser meets the owner to discuss value and verify the information supplied.
  • If they still disagree, each side presents at a public hearing.
  • The board mails its decision inside 30 days of that hearing.
  • The next step is the state Property Tax Commission, where notice is due 30 days from the board's letter and most cases are heard in Raleigh.

The statewide framework is G.S. 105-322. A seller's best exhibits are recent sales of similar homes nearby, any appraisal tied to a sale contract, and repair quotes for defects a mass appraisal cannot see.

sections.h2: Which payment methods does Henderson County accept?
sections.html:
Owners can mail a check, visit the counter, pay online or use the automated phone line. The counter takes cash, check, money order and cards. A drop box in the south parking lot is emptied daily, and it is no place for cash.

  • Card and e-check users pay a convenience fee that goes to the payment vendor.
  • Prepayments taken January through July appear as a credit once the bill is issued.
  • Owners who expect to be late are asked to call before delinquency, and most are offered a plan.
  • Mail checks to Henderson County Tax Collector, 200 N Grove St, Ste 66, Hendersonville, NC 28792.

The state calendar, due September 1 with par payment until January 6 and interest after that, is in G.S. 105-360.

sections.h2: What relief programs are open to Henderson County homeowners?
sections.html:
Residents 65 or over make up 29.1% of the county, so the age-based programs reach many owners. The tax pages list the elderly or permanently disabled exclusion, the disabled veterans exclusion, present-use value and the circuit-breaker deferral, all handled by the Assessor.

  • Elderly or disabled: $25,000 or half the value of the permanent residence, whichever is greater, if 2026 income is within $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 off appraised value, no age or income cap.
  • Circuit breaker: tax held to 4.0% of income, or 5.0% above the $38,800 mark up to $58,200, with the excess deferred.

Only one of the three can be used by a given owner. Apply on Form AV-9, which the county accepts through June 1 before the tax year. A circuit-breaker deferral is payable when the home transfers.

sections.h2: Which Census figures matter for Henderson County owners?
sections.html:
Census Bureau data frame the household base behind a Henderson County sale.

  • Land area of 372.95 square miles, with 311.8 residents per square mile counted in 2020.
  • 51,067 households for 2020-2024, averaging 2.29 persons.
  • Population estimate of 122,375 on July 1, 2025, a 5.2% rise from the 2020 base.
  • A $1,187 median gross rent and 7,811 veterans.
  • Degree attainment: 36.5% of those 25 and up hold a four-year degree or more.
  • 2022 retail sales of $2,287,875 thousand, plus $1,199,447 thousand in health care and social services receipts.

Commutes average 22.5 minutes, and nearly nine in ten residents (89.7%) were in the same home a year before the survey.

sections.h2: What follows unpaid Henderson County tax, and how does it touch a sale?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector may foreclose on real property with delinquent taxes, and sales are held on the courthouse steps at 200 North Grove Street. The county lists each parcel with an estimated opening bid that does not include interest and expenses accruing daily. Upset bid amounts are available from the Clerk of Court at 828-694-4100, and sale questions go to 828-698-3090.

The sale posted on the county page was May 27, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. and listed 15 parcels with estimated opening bids from $739.08 up to $14,077.24.

A seller with a balance can clear it at closing instead. Get the payoff from the Tax Collector, and expect the deed excise tax of $1.00 per $500 to be paid separately by the seller. On pricing, Census figures show owner-occupied homes with a median value of $351,400, 75.0% owner occupancy, household income at a $68,187 median and 1,093 permits issued in 2025 (Census QuickFacts).

faqs.q: When is the Henderson County reappraisal effective?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027. The county's last reappraisal was in 2023 and it follows a four-year cycle, so values reset to market as of that date.

faqs.q: By when must a 2027 Henderson County value be contested?
faqs.a: The county schedule shows the Board of Equalization and Review adjourning and closing the 2027 appeal period on May 14, 2027. Informal appeals to the Assessor run from January 1 to April 13, 2027.

faqs.q: Can I pay Henderson County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. The Tax Collector encourages monthly installments, accepts prepayments from January through July, and usually offers a payment plan if you call before the bill is delinquent.

faqs.q: Where are Henderson County tax foreclosure sales held?
faqs.a: On the courthouse steps at 200 North Grove Street, Hendersonville. The Tax Collector's page lists each parcel and an estimated opening bid, and the Clerk of Court gives current upset bid amounts.

faqs.q: Who sets the Henderson County tax rate?
faqs.a: The Board of Commissioners sets the county rate, and each municipality sets its own. The Assessor only determines value, so an appeal changes the value and not the rate.
